prompt:
Create an authoritative, highly engaging 8-card modern presentation about:
Title: "Accident Prevention and Highway Safety"
Target Language: English
Tone & Style: modern, informative, authoritative public safety guidance
Context & Description: Practical guidelines on defensive driving, blind spots, and helmet compliance for highway motorists.

=== PRESENTATION STRUCTURE & CARD OUTLINE ===
Card 1: Accident Prevention and Highway Safety
• Subtitle: Practical guidelines on defensive driving, blind spots, and helmet compliance for highway motorists.
• Presented by: RakshAI Public Safety Initiative
• Language: EN | Format: MODERN Presentation Deck
• Focus: Actionable preparedness, rapid decision making, and life preservation
[Design & Imagery]: Visual Style: Crisp infographic illustration showing a bold modern cover title card with high-contrast emergency lighting, clean icons, and authoritative safety typography.
[Key Takeaway]: Key Takeaway: Rapid emergency readiness saves lives. Every second counts.

Card 2: Introduction & Urgent Importance
• Context: Practical guidelines on defensive driving, blind spots, and helmet compliance for highway motorists.
• Every year, thousands of critical delays occur due to hesitation and lack of verified contact info.
• The 'Golden Hour' principle: Prompt intervention in the first 60 minutes cuts mortality rates by over 50%.
• Immediate bystander safety: Ensuring the scene is secure before initiating help.
[Design & Imagery]: Visual Style: Crisp infographic illustration showing a split diagram depicting the timeline of emergency triage and the golden-hour survival rate graph.
[Key Takeaway]: Key Takeaway: Early situational recognition prevents compound disasters.

Card 3: Key Principles & Safety Framework
• 1. Assess the scene: Identify active fire, electrical leakage, traffic, or toxic smoke.
• 2. Alert authorities immediately via 112 (Universal Emergency) before attempting solo rescues.
• 3. Direct crowd control: Assign specific individuals to clear pathways and guide incoming ambulances.
• 4. Preserve vitals: Keep the patient warm, airway clear, and avoid moving suspect spinal injuries.
[Design & Imagery]: Visual Style: Crisp infographic illustration showing four sequential safety checkpoint icons with high-visibility hazard badges.
[Key Takeaway]: Key Takeaway: Safety first: never become a second casualty during rescue.

Card 4: Step-by-Step Emergency Action Plan
• Phase 1: Dial 112 / 108 / 101 with exact GPS coordinates and landmark references.
• Phase 2: Communicate caller name, patient count, conscious status, and visible hazards clearly.
• Phase 3: Deploy available first-aid (direct pressure for bleeding, recovery position for unconscious breathing).
• Phase 4: Station a volunteer at the main road junction to guide response vehicles.
[Design & Imagery]: Visual Style: Crisp infographic illustration showing a clean modern flowchart illustrating 4 phases of emergency execution.
[Key Takeaway]: Key Takeaway: Clear, calm communication is the primary bridge to rapid hospital dispatch.

Card 5: Technology & Community Coordination
• RakshAI Automated Assistance: Instant nearest hospital & fire station geofencing.
• Smart Corridors: Traffic signal coordination for emergency vehicles to bypass bottlenecks.
• Live GPS Share: Seamlessly sending one-tap maps location to family and responders.
• Offline Directory Backup: Accessing vital phone numbers even when cellular data is severed.
[Design & Imagery]: Visual Style: Crisp infographic illustration showing a mobile interface graphic showing smart ambulance telemetry and digital SOS routing.
[Key Takeaway]: Key Takeaway: Technology augments community response when integrated seamlessly.

Card 6: Critical Pitfalls & What to Avoid
• DO NOT crowd the casualty or restrict fresh airflow.
• DO NOT give liquids or water to an unconscious or heavily bleeding person (aspiration risk).
• DO NOT move an accident victim with suspected cervical/spinal injury unless immediate fire/explosion danger exists.
• DO NOT delay dialing 112 to take photos or record videos for social media.
[Design & Imagery]: Visual Style: Crisp infographic illustration showing red warning icons with concise 'Do Not' annotations for emergency errors.
[Key Takeaway]: Key Takeaway: Preventing common bystander mistakes is as vital as active aid.

Card 7: Readiness Checklist & Emergency Kit
• Keep a 72-hour family emergency kit (water, non-perishables, flashlight, whistle, first-aid).
• Store emergency numbers in phone ICE (In Case of Emergency) contacts.
• Conduct regular household and office fire drills and identify 2 evacuation routes.
• Have basic bleeding control kits (sterile gauze, elastic bandages, tourniquet) in every vehicle.
[Design & Imagery]: Visual Style: Crisp infographic illustration showing an exploded view of an emergency trauma kit with labeled medical tools.
[Key Takeaway]: Key Takeaway: Preparedness in calm times guarantees swift action during crises.

Card 8: Summary & Life-Saving Contacts
• Universal Emergency Helpline: Dial 112 (24/7 National Emergency)
• Ambulance Services: 108 (Trauma/Emergency) | 102 (Free Transport)
• Fire & Rescue: 101 | Police Control: 100
• Empower your community with RakshAI: Stay alert, stay prepared, save lives.
[Design & Imagery]: Visual Style: Crisp infographic illustration showing a bold emergency card featuring prominent national helpline badges and RakshAI branding.
[Key Takeaway]: Key Takeaway: Save these numbers in your phone now. Preparedness starts today.

=== INSTRUCTIONS FOR GAMMA AI ===
- Output language: Write card titles and body text in clear, professional English.
- Visual theme: Apply a clean, modern modern aesthetic with emergency red and amber accents.
- Structure: Keep bullet points punchy and easy to scan from a distance.
- End the deck with universal emergency phone numbers (112, 108, 101, 100).
